reason: A burr is a dispersal unit with hooked spines, but what it is varies by taxon: a fruit, an involucre of bristles round spikelets (Cenchrus), or a whole cyme or infructescence ('each cyme falls as a complete burr'). Only 'present' is stated. Without the taxon it cannot be grounded to one class.

Narrower name. In mosses the urn is the spore-bearing body of the capsule below the operculum. PO lists 'moss capsule' as a synonym of sporangium, and its lid is spore capsule operculum PO_0030044, so the urn is the capsule without its lid. Ribbing, smoothness, colour and length of the urn are the capsule's.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of perichaetal bract (PO_0030030)
reason: Cells of the perichaetial leaves of mosses. PO has perichaetal bract PO_0030030 and plant cell PO_0009002, so this is the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern: shape (rhomboidal, elongate) and papillosity of the cells of that bract.

label: peristome basal membrane
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0030042 peristome
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a moss peristome (PO:0030042) that is the continuous membrane formed by the fused lower portions of the inner (endostome) segments, from which the segments and cilia arise. NOTE: PO has peristome PO:0030042 and peristome tooth PO:0030043 but no basal membrane; propose to PO with the other bryophyte capsule parts.
reason: A standard bryological structure. Its presence or absence, height (projecting, rudimentary), hyalinity and striation are diagnostic in moss floras. Peristome base alone cannot express 'basal membrane absent', because a membrane being absent is not the same as the peristome having no base. Propose upstream to PO.

Exact synonym: PO lists 'hermaphrodite flower' as a synonym of flower PO_0009046. It probably failed to ground because of the French plural or the split form ('3–4 hermaphrodite and fertile'). The bisexual sense is carried by the word, not by a separate class.
A unit of length (µm; 'fi' and '/*' are OCR of µ). It belongs with the measurement, as 'μm' did in the previous review.
A quality, FLOPO:0991078 pinnatifid. '2–3-pinnatifid' is its degree, not a part to count.
Exact synonym: PO lists 'ovulate cone' as a synonym of megasporangiate strobilus PO_0005032. This matches the rule for 'seed cone' (C378).
A unit of time (leaf life span, flowering and maturation periods, chilling requirement). It is not a plant structure.

label: crownshaft
parent: is_a PO_0025269 collective organ part structure; part_of PO_0009006 shoot system
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) composed of the tubular leaf sheaths (PO:0020104) of the uppermost leaves of a palm, which tightly enclose one another to form a smooth, often coloured column at the top of the stem (PO:0009047), below the leaf crown. NOTE: No crownshaft in PO; modelled like ochrea (collective of leaf parts).
reason: A real palm structure. Its presence ('crownshaft present', 'prominent green crownshaft') is a key character in palm floras. Leaf sheath alone cannot state that the sheaths form a crownshaft. Propose upstream to PO.

Narrower name: a gland seen as a dot in or on the lamina or perianth. It follows rule C265 (gland → portion of secretory tissue). Their density and colour ('6–10 /mm²', 'dark') are those of the glands. The surface quality is the separate value FLOPO gland-dotted.
An adverb, a fragment of 'pairs of strongly ascending nerves'. The counted part is the vein.

A narrow segment of whatever organ is being described: calyx or corolla lobes (often in Flora do Brasil), leaf segments or perianth segments. It is generic, like 'segment', which the previous review rejected because it needs the organ it belongs to.
A quality (PATO:0104355 ascending), a fragment of 'ascending teeth' or 'ascending lateral veins'.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) as the apex region of the lobe of the described organ: calyx lobe (FLOPO_0986005), corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006), perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004) or leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517)
reason: The apex region of a lobe. The region pattern (apex of a qualified whole) expresses it once the lobe's organ is known from the statement's context. If no organ is known, fall back to plant organ apex.

A misspelling or extraction artefact of 'phyllary', which PO lists as a NARROW synonym of involucral bract (rule C250). The examples (acute apices, unequal, glabrous faces) are typical phyllary characters.

label: pollinarium
parent: is_a PO_0009011 plant structure; part_of PO_0009046 flower
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is the unit of pollen transfer in orchids and Apocynaceae, made up of two or more pollinia (FLOPO pollinium) together with the structures joining them, such as caudicles, stipe and viscidium or translator, and removed from the flower as a whole by a pollinator. NOTE: No pollinarium in PO; complements pollinium (FLOPO_0986016), caudicle (FLOPO_0986033) and viscidium (FLOPO_0986032).
reason: A real structure that orchid and Apocynaceae floras count and describe ('Pollinaria 2', 'straight'). It is distinct from a single pollinium. Propose upstream to PO together with pollinium.
A row is an arrangement of other parts (scales, cells, spines, seeds). The number of rows is a quality of what is arranged in them, and that part must come from the statement.
A quality (blunt or obtuse), a fragment of 'blunt ridges' or 'blunt angles'. The counted part is the ridge or angle.
The stalk of a fern sporangium. PO has stalk PO_0025066 and sporangium PO_0025094, so the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern expresses it: glands and hairs on the stalk of the sporangium.
A length-to-width ratio phrase, not a structure. It is handled like 'ratio' in the previous review.

In these moss descriptions the capsule cells are the exothecial cells ('exothecial cells short-rectangular'). PO has exothecium PO_0030073 (sporangium epidermis), so this is plant cell as part of that tissue.
The degree of branching of an inflorescence or axis is a quality of the branched structure, not a part. The bearer is the inflorescence or axis named in the statement.
A counting context ('bracts 1–2 per pedicel'), like 'per node' and 'per flower' in the previous review. The counted part is the bract or bracteole.

label: perichaetium
parent: is_a PO_0025023 collective phyllome structure; part_of PO_0030018 gametophore
definition: A collective phyllome structure (PO:0025023) of a bryophyte gametophore (PO:0030018) composed of the perichaetal bracts (PO:0030030) that surround a cluster of archegonia and later the base of the sporophyte seta. NOTE: PO has perichaetal bract PO:0030030 but no class for the whole perichaetium.
reason: A real structure. Moss floras describe its position ('terminal on axillary branches'), size and number, which belong to the whole and not to one bract. Propose upstream to PO beside perichaetal bract.
A positional quality (on the side toward the base of the rachis), a fragment of 'basiscopic pinnules' or 'basiscopic nerves'. The counted part is the pinnule or vein.
Narrower name: a gland, following rule C265. 'Circular' is its shape (PATO circular) and should be split off as the quality. The count applies to the gland.
A shape quality (conical), a fragment of 'conic prickles' or 'conic projection'. The part is the prickle or projection.

An auricle of whatever organ is being described: the leaf base, stipules, a grass sheath (PO_0020106 leaf sheath auricle covers only that case) or a calyx or corolla. It is generic and needs the organ it belongs to, like 'claw' and 'horn' in the previous review.
A fragment of '3-sect' or '3–5-sect', meaning dissected into that many segments: PATO:0104362 dissected (or FLOPO pinnatisect when pinnate). It is a quality, not a part.
